summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with fevers, dysuria, hematuria, and syncope following capping of her nephrostomy tube, concerning for a urinary tract infection in the setting of a renal transplant. She was treated empirically with IV linezolid and ceftriaxone, then transitioned to oral cefpodoxime after urine culture identified pan-sensitive Klebsiella. Her symptoms resolved, and she remained afebrile by discharge. Kidney function improved, allowing restart of Lasix at a reduced dose. Myfortic was decreased to reduce immunosuppression, and warfarin was lowered due to supratherapeutic INR. An echocardiogram showed worsened pulmonary hypertension but no new structural abnormalities. She was discharged home on a 14-day course of antibiotics with follow-up planned in transplant and cardiology clinics.
problems: Urinary tract infection, site not specified
